page_title: Hey Mac: Face Unlock for Mac & App Lock (Free)

sources.entry: Hey Mac - On-device face unlock for the lock screen and privacy shields for selected apps. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/iharshitmaurya/HeyMac) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Hey Mac
summary.one_liner: Hey Mac is a free, open-source macOS app that adds on-device face unlock to the Mac lock screen and can blur or lock individual apps until the user is verified.
use_cases: Unlock a Mac lock screen by looking at the screen
Lock private apps like Messages, Notes or Mail behind face verification
Blur a window or the whole display so others cannot read it
Require re-verification for an app after a set time
Install an open-source face unlock tool via Homebrew
summary.what_it_does: Hey Mac uses the Mac's built-in camera to recognize the user's face and unlock the lock screen when they look at it, with no password needed. It can lock any chosen app so that others see a blur until the user verifies with face, Touch ID, or password. For each app, the user can choose to require unlock on every launch, after 5 to 15 minutes, or whenever they switch away. Face recognition runs on the Mac using the Apple Neural Engine, and the app keeps only encrypted face data in the Keychain, never saving a photo. A built-in liveness check aims to reject photos and screens held to the camera. The source code is published on GitHub under the MIT license.
notable: Face recognition and face data stay on the Mac; no servers, accounts, or saved photos
App Lock blurs whole display or only the locked window, with per-app relock timing
Open source under MIT license, installable via .dmg or Homebrew cask
Unlock animation drops from the notch (or floats at top on Macs without one)
caveats: Requires Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 Sonoma or later
Not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS shows a warning on first launch and requires Open Anyway in System Settings
Uses the regular camera without a depth sensor, so it is less secure than iPhone Face ID; the page advises keeping a strong Mac password
